paragraphs.source_en: One of the differences between the earlier and later forms is the appearance, in the later phase, of elaborated masks and head covers (Fig. 5-18). Supposing that they were related to rituals or ceremonies, it may be hypothesized that the diversification of masks was related to a change in spiritual life. Did an evolution of rituals, ceremonies and perhaps of the religion occur in this final stage? And what could have been the reason for this transformation?

paragraphs.source_en: An important event took place in the 8th millennium BP in the Central Sahara, namely the arrival of Pastoral populations into the same geographical area as that frequented by the hunter-gatherers who created the Round Heads. This art remained extremely conservative for its whole length but it showed some alteration in its final stages: could this have been a reaction to the newly arrived population, so different economically and probably also culturally? The Pastoral groups also produced paintings; could the evolution of the Round Head art have been a competition with the Pastoral art and a kind of reinforcement of cultural values? The next section presents an hypotheses of what possibly happened with the hunters and their art after the arrival of the pastoralists.
